label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Probability & Statistics)

body.en:
Why Bayes' Theorem & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion Work: Any event \(B\) can be partitioned into disjoint intersections \(B = (B \cap A) \cup (B \cap A')\). By additivity of mutually exclusive events and the multiplication rule \(P(A \cap B) = P(B \mid A)P(A)\):

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{P(B \mid A)P(A)}{P(B \mid A)P(A) + P(B \mid A')P(A')} \]

Similarly, in counting \(|A \cup B|\), summing \(|A| + |B|\) counts every element in \(A \cap B\) twice; subtracting \(|A \cap B|\) once restores exact cardinality: \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)\).

A bag holds 3 red and 5 blue counters. One is drawn at random. Find \( P(\text{red}) \).

There are \( 3+5=8 \) equally likely counters, 3 of them red:

\[ P(\text{red})=\frac{3}{8}. \]

For grouped data with unequal class widths, plot frequency density on the \(y\)-axis, not frequency. \(\text{Frequency density}=\dfrac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}}\). Area of each bar equals the frequency for that class.

A class interval 20–30 has frequency 15; class width = 10.

\[\text{Freq. density}=\frac{15}{10}=1.5.\]

Conversely, a bar of height 2.4 over interval 30–45 (width 15) represents frequency \(2.4\times15=36\).

Without replacement: after removing one item, the total decreases, so probabilities on the second branch change. Conditional probability: \(P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}\). Multiply along branches for "and"; add separate branches for "or".

body.en:
A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Find \(P(\text{both red})\).

\[P(\text{both red})=\frac{5}{8}\times\frac{4}{7}=\frac{20}{56}=\frac{5}{14}.\]

rows.en: Using \(P(A \cap B) = 0\) when told \(A\) and \(B\) are independent
Confuses disjoint (mutually exclusive) events with statistically independent events.
For independent events, multiply probabilities: \(P(A \cap B) = P(A)\cdot P(B)\).
Dividing by the grand total \(N\) when computing \(P(A \mid B)\) from a table
Computes the joint probability \(P(A \cap B)\) instead of conditioning on subset \(B\).
Restrict the denominator strictly to the row/column total of the given condition \(B\).
Using permutations \({}^nP_r\) when selecting a committee with no distinct roles
Overcounts every group of size \(r\) by \(r!\) internal orderings.

body.en: Exam Strategy (Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580 Extended)): Whenever a probability problem involves "at least one" success across multiple trials, immediately use the Complement Rule: \(P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{none})\). It turns a multi-case sum into a single calculation.

body.en:
Histogram Frequency Density: In Cambridge IGCSE histograms, class widths are usually unequal. The vertical axis is ALWAYS Frequency Density, where \(\text{Frequency Density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}\). Frequency is given by the AREA of the bar, not its height!

Probability Without Replacement: When selecting items without replacement, reduce both the numerator and the denominator for the second draw: \(\frac{4}{10} \times \frac{3}{9}\). Forgetting to reduce the denominator to 9 is the classic exam error.

Estimating the Mean from Grouped Data: Always use the midpoint of each class interval, multiply by frequency, sum \(\sum fx\), and divide by total frequency \(\sum f\) (never divide by the number of intervals).

question.en:
The table shows the time, \(t\) minutes, taken by 50 students to complete a homework task.
Intervals: \(0 < t \le 10\) (freq: 8), \(10 < t \le 20\) (freq: 14), \(20 < t \le 30\) (freq: 18), \(30 < t \le 40\) (freq: 10).
Calculate an estimate of the mean time taken.
question.ar:
The table shows the time, \(t\) minutes, taken by 50 students to compليكنe a homework task.
Intervals: \(0 < t \le 10\) (freq: 8), \(10 < t \le 20\) (freq: 14), \(20 < t \le 30\) (freq: 18), \(30 < t \le 40\) (freq: 10).
احسب an estimate of the mean time taken.

solution.en:
Find class midpoints (\(x\)) and products (\(fx\)):

  • Midpoint 5: \(8 \times 5 = 40\)
  • Midpoint 15: \(14 \times 15 = 210\)
  • Midpoint 25: \(18 \times 25 = 450\)
  • Midpoint 35: \(10 \times 35 = 350\)
\[\sum fx = 40 + 210 + 450 + 350 = 1050\]\[\text{Estimated Mean} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{1050}{50} = 21\text{ minutes}\]
